This message comes from Kachava. A little boost goes a long way, especially when it comes to caring for your gut during the holiday season and beyond.
Introducing Kachava's new 3-in-1 digestive boost. Simply mix in to your favorite Kachava shake or any cold beverage.
Go to Kachava.com and use code NPR for 15% off your first order. That's K-A-C-H-A-V-A.com. Code NPR.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
The U.S. House could be voting this week on whether to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. A short time ago, Republican Congressman Thomas Massie
reintroduced articles of impeachment for high crimes and misdemeanors. Among other charges, Massie accuses Hegseth of
illegally waging war against Iran and ignoring laws intended to minimize civilian casualties.
He was very effective at killing school children in Iran. He was very effective at extrajudicial killings.
There's no argument in these impeachment articles that he's ineffective.
The argument here is that he's broken laws and he's violated the Constitution.
On the war, Hegseth predicts history will judge President Trump, quote, "very kindly."
In Newport, Rhode Island today, the Defense Secretary said, like the president,
he thinks going to war was the right thing to do before Iran could build a nuclear weapon.
As the president points out so clearly, you can't let crazy Islamists have a nuclear bomb.
And so the choice was don't act and wish it away or take a bold move, which the president did with Midnight Hammer,
which we've done with Epic Fury. And I think it was the right step.
It has been a strong day for tech stocks with one major exception, NVIDIA.
The chip making company that's long led the A.I. stock market boom saw its stock value drop 4.9 percent.
Here's N.P.R. Stephen Besaha.
NVIDIA is investigating its CEO, Jensen Wong, after news outlets reported he had an affair with a possible Chinese spy.
But NVIDIA's drama has been overshadowed by traders' shifting feelings about what the midterm elections mean for tech stocks.
They've swung up and down since election night, most recently swinging up, NVIDIA not included.
Lower oil prices also calm investors. Crude oil futures are down about 4.5 percent and selling at about $86 a barrel.
That follows the Trump administration signaling restraint in terms of future strikes against Iran.
Stephen Besaha, NPR News.
The French government's alleging that Iran's Revolutionary Guard was behind last month's cyber attack
that hacked hundreds of supermarket refrigeration systems across the country.
Iran has yet to respond to the accusations. Here's Rebecca Rossman.
The French foreign minister called the attack "unprecedented" and suggested Iran would face more EU sanctions.
The Paris prosecutor's office, meanwhile, says it has opened an investigation into a cyber unit linked to Iran's Revolutionary Guard.
It began in October with a cyber attack on some 700 commercial fridges and freezers across France,
sending temperatures soaring to over 120 degrees Fahrenheit.
Some fridges even caught fire.
Supermarkets were forced to throw away millions of dollars worth of spoiled food.
Last week, other countries in Europe were hit with similar attacks.
It's unclear if the incidents are linked.
Rebecca Rossman, NPR News, Paris.
On Wall Street, the markets ended the day higher, 2 percent to more than 2.5 percent.
You're listening to NPR News.
Pope Leo has met with survivors of clergy sexual abuse during his visit to Argentina today.
The Vatican says the pontiff spent about an hour meeting five victims, first individually and then as a group.
His meeting was part of a broader trip to Latin America where his agenda also included a visit to Peru.
New research points to the role of circadian rhythms in depression.
The study from a team at the University of Sydney suggests that as many as one in four people with a diagnosis
could have a distinct type of depression rooted in problems with their circadian rhythms.
More from NPR's Will Stone.
The study used a database of about 10,000 adults in Australia with depression.
The researchers came up with different criteria.
They looked at sleep schedule, whether people were a night owl, their level of tiredness in the morning and more.
Based on that, they found just under 25 percent of adults fit this profile for circadian depression.
A key finding was that they tended to have less success with SSRIs, the most commonly prescribed class of antidepressants.
The study was published in the British Journal of Psychiatry.
The authors emphasize the study is a proof of concept and needs to be replicated in other populations.
But it could eventually help steer patients to treatments that are more likely to work.
Will Stone, NPR News.
Ohio State University is temporarily suspending the Sigma Alpha Epsilon fraternity,
while authorities investigate a video circulating online that appears to show two apparently panicked men with their clothes on fire.
The university spokesman says the men are receiving medical care.
The Dow's closed up more than 1,100 points or more than 2 percent.
This is NPR News.
